failures.criterion: AC4 / Requirement 5 and 7: a launch into a running drifted pod keeps the pod, and the role runs there until the round replaces it. The role must actually be able to run in the pod the launch keeps.
failures.evidence:
RED TEST: packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/drift_launch_test.go, TestARoleStartedInAKeptDriftedPodIsStartedAsItsPodWasBuilt, committed at 4d0048de9f11 on legion/INFRA-484. Command: `cd packages/daemon && go test ./internal/runtime/sandbox -run TestARoleStartedInAKeptDriftedPodIsStartedAsItsPodWasBuilt -count=1`. Both rows FAIL at that head.

Row 'the secrets broker's enrollment': the start the kept pod's launcher is sent carries [--agent-secrets-key-dir /var/run/legion/agent-secrets --pod-token-file /var/run/legion/agent-secrets-token/token --agent-secrets-bin /opt/legion/bin/agent-secrets], because launcher.go:424-425 adds the three flags whenever the runtime enrolls, while the kept pod carries neither the agent-secrets-token volume nor agent-secrets-key-tester (measured pod volume list: issue, provision, tmp, config, the per-role launcher/private/state/gh set, role-homes, providers). `legion worker-shim` stats --agent-secrets-key-dir and --pod-token-file and exits 1 when either is absent (packages/daemon/internal/shim/config.go:121-130, held by cmd/legion config_test.go:163-167), so Oh My Pi is never spawned.

Row 'a named role's overlay': the generation-2 start's PI_CONFIG_FILES is '/etc/legion-operator-roles/fallback.yml' while the kept pod does not mount operator-roles. The repository states the consequence itself at roleconfig_test.go:160-161: the role's Oh My Pi 'would refuse to start' on it.

Why this blocks rather than being an accepted consequence of keeping the pod: a process that cannot start never registers, so its claim never answers the round. daemon/podupdate.go's blockingClaims makes every claim of the pod that has a session block the round, and supervise/table.go:1499-1505 (askForUpdate) revives a suspended claim into that same pod to hand it the update task. So the round that exists to replace the pod is blocked by the pod it is replacing, and only an operator drain ends it. Before this change these three facets were movedInPod, read StaleAddress, and the launch replaced the pod, so the role always started in a pod that could run it.

Scope: the two facets this test drives, movedRoleOverlays and movedEnrollment. The third, movedSessionStore, is not a regression: the generation gets OMP_SESSION_SQL_DSN_FILE=/var/run/legion/providers/OMP_SESSION_SQL_DSN, which the old pod projects from the old key, so the role reads the old store in the kept pod and the new store after the replacement, where its session is absent exactly as R8 says, and that was true before this change too (measured in the same probe run).

The implementer's own tests do not catch it: TestAddingARoleOverlaysMountDriftsAnIssuePodMadeWithoutIt (roleconfig_test.go:196-203) and TestAPodEnrolledOtherwiseThanTheRuntimeIsNowHasDrifted (restage_test.go:488-498) both Resume into the kept pod and assert only that the pod was kept; neither reads the start command the kept pod is handed.

The architect's question on suspensions (no new suspension of a role): read, not run. The displaced roles are resumed uncharged on their own sessions, as for a pod a launch replaces.
